title: Principles one to five
hook: God exists, is one, has no body, is eternal, and alone is to be worshiped

segments.voice: Yesterday, your line: thirteen principles. This week left the sea of the Talmud and met Maimonides: his young book on the road, and the list of foundations inside it. Which line from the list stayed with you? Today, its first stretch. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-four.

One what? It's a question a child might ask, and Maimonides takes it seriously. Behind it stands a line from Deuteronomy that Jewish prayer comes back to morning and night: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." His list builds on it, and takes up the child's questions one by one. One like a single apple is one? One like a team is one? And if the Torah talks about God's hand and God's eyes, does God have hands and eyes? His first five foundations are his answers. Today, the stretch of the list about God.
screen: `THE LORD IS ONE.` → `ONE LIKE WHAT?` → `FIVE FOUNDATIONS ABOUT GOD.`

segments.voice: Principles one to five. The first: God exists, and everything else exists because of God. Not the other way around. The world leans on God; God doesn't lean on the world. The second: God is one. And here Maimonides is careful. Not one like one of a pair, and not one like one member of a kind. Not one like a single body, which can still be cut into parts. A oneness, he says, unlike any other oneness. The third: God has no body. So what about the hand of God, the eyes of the LORD? He reads them as the Torah speaking in human language, so that people can understand. Deuteronomy reminds Israel that at Sinai they heard a voice but saw no form at all. The fourth: God is eternal. Before everything, after everything. In Isaiah's words: "I am the first, and I am the last." The fifth: only God is to be worshiped. Not the stars, not angels, not any power in between, as if God needed a go-between. Prayer goes straight to God. Now put them side by side. Each one takes something away. God isn't caused. God isn't many. God isn't a body. God doesn't begin or end. God doesn't need a messenger. Maimonides teaches God, here, mostly by saying what God is not. One, bodiless, eternal.
screen: `GOD EXISTS, AND ALL ELSE LEANS ON GOD.` · `ONE, UNLIKE ANY OTHER ONE.` · `NO BODY, NO FORM.` · `ETERNAL, AND WORSHIPED ALONE.` · then, large: `ONE, BODILESS, ETERNAL.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to sit with one word: one. Settle, and let your breath find its own pace. On the in-breath, let the word arrive: one. On the out-breath, let it go. When a picture comes with it, a number, a shape, a face, notice it, and let it pass without holding on. Maimonides kept taking pictures away. You can try the same, gently, for a few breaths. If you pray, you can say the line from Deuteronomy once, quietly. Then just the breath. The bell holds the time.
Principles one to five. The first stretch of Maimonides' list: God exists, is one, has no body, is eternal, and alone is to be worshiped. Today's word.
Your line: one, bodiless, eternal. Today, when you catch yourself picturing something too small for the word God, notice it, and let one picture go. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-four.

howItsDone: Jews say the Shema, "Hear, O Israel," in the morning and evening prayers and at bedtime; Maimonides' first principles are often taught alongside it, and his explanations of them are studied in his commentary and in the opening chapters of the Mishneh Torah.
